info.summary: Multi-tennant application managing CRUD operations on our Products

get.summary: Get latest revisions of all products
get.description: Returns a collection of the latest (or latest approved) revision for each product, fully resolved with knowledge units, knowledge topics, and product families. For a faster list-view response use **GET /slim** instead.

200.description: Retrieve the latest revision for all products

post.description: Creates a new product with the provided details. Returns the created product with a unique ID and history ID.
Creates a copy of an existing product, optionally including its content.

get.summary: Get latest revisions of all products (slim)
get.description: Returns a lightweight collection of the latest revision for each product. `knowledge_units` and `knowledge_topics` are omitted entirely. `product_families` are returned as shallow identity refs (`_id` + `product_family_history_id`) only, with no nested data. Recommended for frontend list views where full nesting is not required.

200.description: Retrieve a lightweight list of the latest revision for all products

Results are returned in request order; a single failed item does not fail the batch.

ApplyUnderlyingSchemaResponse.title: ApplyUnderlyingSchemaResponse
ApplyUnderlyingSchemaResponse.description:
Response for the 'Apply Underlying Schema' action on a Product KU.

Pulls the LATEST APPROVED revision of the Schema Library schema this
Product KU is "auto based on" down onto the Product KU: existing
Knowledge Topics that still match a schema topic get their
name/form updated in place (their data is never touched), and schema
topics with no existing match get created as brand new Knowledge
Topics. Product Knowledge Topics that no longer have any counterpart in
the schema's latest approved revision are left untouched - this action
never removes content from the Product KU. A draft (unapproved) schema
revision is never eligible, no matter how new.

applied_ku_schema_history_id/applied_ku_schema_id/applied_ku_schema_version
identify the approved schema revision that was applied.

KnowledgeTopicUpdate.title: KnowledgeTopicUpdate
KnowledgeTopicUpdate.description:
Model for updating a Knowledge Topic.

Only allows updating:
- knowledge_topic_name: The name of the knowledge topic
- knowledge_topic_schema: The schema definition (form structure)
- data: The actual data stored in the topic

Excluded fields (immutable/system-managed):
- knowledge_unit_history_id: Ownership relationship (immutable)
- product_history_id: Ownership relationship (immutable)
- type: Fundamental characteristic (immutable)
- product_data_collection_id: Tied to type and relationships (immutable)
- source_schema_id: Historical reference (immutable)
- metadata: System-managed tenant metadata (immutable)
- audit_info: System-managed audit trail (auto-updated by service)

UnderlyingSchemaApplyStatus.title: UnderlyingSchemaApplyStatus
UnderlyingSchemaApplyStatus.description:
Whether the Product KU's current KT forms differ from the LATEST
APPROVED revision of its underlying Schema Library schema - i.e.
whether 'Apply Underlying Schema' would actually change anything, and
precisely which KTs would be created/updated. Unlike
UnderlyingSchemaSyncStatus, a KT with no counterpart in the schema is
never reported here (Apply never removes anything), and the comparison
revision is always the strictly-approved one - never a draft, never a
fallback to the latest revision.

UnderlyingSchemaSyncStatus.title: UnderlyingSchemaSyncStatus
UnderlyingSchemaSyncStatus.description:
Whether the Product KU's current name/description/KT forms differ from
the COMPARISON revision of its underlying Schema Library schema - the
latest approved version (e.g. 2.0, 3.0) when one exists, otherwise (for
schemas still under 1.0) the latest revision - i.e. whether 'Update
Underlying Schema' would actually change anything, and precisely which
KU/KT-level changes it would make. Drives whether the FE shows the update
button, and lets the confirm dialog list only the entities that will
actually change instead of everything unconditionally. A content diff,
not a version comparison.

UnderlyingSchemaSyncTopic.title: UnderlyingSchemaSyncTopic
UnderlyingSchemaSyncTopic.description:
One Knowledge Topic that 'Update Underlying Schema' would actually
change - updating its existing Knowledge Topic Schema counterpart
("update"), creating a brand new one because it has no trace ("new"), or
removing a schema entry that no longer has any corresponding Product
Knowledge Topic ("remove", e.g. the KT was deleted from the Product).

For "remove", knowledge_topic_history_id/knowledge_topic_name describe
the Knowledge Topic Schema being removed (there is no Product KT anymore
to describe it from).

UpdateKnowledgeTopicSchema.description: Model for updating a knowledge topic schema

UpdateUnderlyingSchemaResponse.title: UpdateUnderlyingSchemaResponse
UpdateUnderlyingSchemaResponse.description:
Response for the 'Update Underlying Schema' action on a Product KU.

Pushes the Product KU's current name/description/KT forms into a new
draft revision of the Schema Library schema it was "auto based on".
new_ku_schema_history_id/new_ku_schema_id/new_ku_schema_version identify
that freshly created draft revision.

UseCaseConfigView.title: UseCaseConfigView
UseCaseConfigView.description:
Bundled use-case enrichment for one KT: the purple trace columns plus the
completeness-banner status, grouped under a single field on the KT response.

Grouping (rather than two sibling fields) keeps future additions — ordering,
validation rules, etc. — from growing the top-level KT shape. Present only for
multi_record topics that belong to a use case; None otherwise.

UseCaseStatusView.title: UseCaseStatusView
UseCaseStatusView.description: Pre-computed completeness banner for one use case the topic belongs to.
